newsitem.title: USA: World Bank to end any corruption-tainted projects.
newsitem.headline: World Bank to end any corruption-tainted projects.

text.p: World Bank President James Wolfensohn vowed on Thursday to cancel any project by the institution in which corruption is discovered.

Speaking to reporters on the final day of the annual meeting of the IMF and World Bank, Wolfensohn said "where there are projects to which we are involved and we find evidence of corruption we will cancel the project."
He added "We are anxious to put teeth in to what we're doing over issues in which we have control."

He conceeded that the Bank could not become a moral policeman or that such efforts would change human behavior overnight but he said that by putting a spotlight on the problem pressure could be generated within countries to make changes.
He told reporters by taking a stand there already had been a strong positive reaction from a number of countries.
But Wolfensohn also made clear that this was a worldwide problem in which wealthy industrial countries in efforts to do business in the developing world had added to the climate of corruption.
"As one of the (Bank) governors said, you have a corrupted and you have a corruptee," Wolfensohn told reporters.
